message.content:
Here’s a quick snapshot of some of the most celebrated American composers across different eras:

| Era | Composer | Notable Works |
|-----|----------|---------------|
| **Early 20th Century** | **John Philip Sousa** (1854‑1932) | “The Stars and Stripes Forever,” “Washington Post March” |
| | **George Gershwin** (1898‑1937) | “Rhapsody in Blue,” “An American in Paris” |
| | **Aaron Copland** (1900‑1990) | “Appalachian Spring,” “Fanfare for the Common Man” |
| | **Samuel Barber** (1910‑1981) | “Adagio for Strings,” “Knoxville: Summer of 1915” |
| | **Leonard Bernstein** (1918‑1990) | “West Side Story,” “Candide” |
| **Mid‑20th Century** | **Philip Glass** (born 1937) | “Einstein on the Beach,” “Glassworks” |
| | **Steve Reich** (born 1936) | “Music for 18 Musicians,” “Different Trains” |
| | **John Adams** (born 1947) | “Short Ride in a Fast Machine,” “Nixon in China” |
| | **William Grant Still** (1895‑1978) | “Afro-American Symphony,” “Bluebird of Happiness” |
| **Contemporary** | **John Williams** (born 1950) | Film scores: “Star Wars,” “Jurassic Park,” “Indiana Jones” |
| | **Hans Zimmer** (born 1957) | “Inception,” “The Dark Knight,” “Interstellar” |
| | **Jennifer Higdon** (born 1962) | “Blue Cathedral,” “Piano Concerto” |

These composers have shaped not only American classical music but also popular culture through film scores, Broadway shows, and modern minimalism.
